 RBI May Hike Rates by 25-50 Bps in December, Banks to Benefit from Easing Oil Prices: Jefferies
 Global brokerage Jefferies predicts a potential 25-50 basis point hike in the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) repo rate at its December monetary policy meeting. This move is anticipated as system liquidity surplus moderates, following the RBI's efforts to absorb excess funds through various operations. The report suggests this rate hike could occur after Diwali and before the Union Budget and state elections in early 2027.
 Indian banks are expected to see improved margins due to easing crude oil prices and bond yields. While credit growth, which stood strong at 18% year-on-year in October 2026, is projected to moderate to 14-16% by March 2027, this shift could enhance banks' loan mix and profitability. Corporate and agricultural lending were key drivers of recent credit expansion. Deposit growth has also shown improvement, reaching 17% year-on-year, boosted by strong inflows under the FCNR-B scheme. These factors, combined with a moderated liquidity environment, paint a picture of cautious optimism for the banking sector.
